part: right hip bracket of a hip exoskeleton: bolts to the waist belt at its top and carries the hip actuator stator at its bottom; the thigh link turns on the actuator output, on the body side of the bracket
frame: mm. x lateral (outward from the body), y anterior, z up. Origin at the centre of the two belt bolts, on the belt contact face (x=0). Hip flexion is a positive rotation about +x (theta=0: link points down; positive moves it anterior).
design_file: Python file defining AXIS=(y,z) of the actuator axis in mm, BUILD_DIR (print layer normal: one of +x,-x,+y,-y,+z,-z) and build() returning one build123d solid in this frame. Nothing else is read.

material.name: printed PA6-CF, 100% infill (ASSUMED values, not from a datasheet)

claims.G1_solid: build() returns exactly one valid closed solid
claims.G2_printer: fits the 250 x 210 bed and 220 mm height with layers normal to BUILD_DIR
claims.G3_keepout: no material outside the envelope, below x=-14 (body), in the belt plate, in the actuator body (r<46, x in [10,58] about AXIS), or in the link hub (r<22, x in [-13,-5])
claims.G4_interfaces: belt bores (r 2.75) and actuator bolt bores (r 2.25 on r=35) and the shaft bore (r 20) are clear; belt seats (r 2.75..6, x 0..3) and the actuator seat (r 21..44, x 7..10, less the bolt bores) are solid
claims.G5_axis: AXIS within y in [-15,15], z in [-115,-75]
claims.G6_stops: the link (hub r22 plus a 26 mm bar to r=170 in x in [-13,-5]) is stopped by the bracket at or before +140 deg flexion and at or before -35 deg extension, and turns freely at 0 deg
claims.K1_rom: for every scenario: the link stays clear of the stops over the exo joint range the MuJoCo run reaches, plus 3 deg each way
claims.K2_cuff_slide: for every scenario: the cuff slides at most 25 mm from its fitted position along the link
claims.S1_strength: for every scenario: safety factor >= 2.0 on both in-plane von Mises (vs 70 MPa) and interlayer tension (vs 35 MPa) at every FEA integration point, at every time sample
claims.S3_stiffness: for every scenario: the actuator seat moves <= 1.0 mm and tilts <= 1.5 deg (best-fit rigid motion of the seat)

scenarios.note: walk = level or sloped walking (4 s, judged from 0.5 s to 3.7 s); sts = sit-to-stand from a chair (3 s, judged 0.5 s to 2.7 s). assist_Nm is the controller gain (delayed-output-feedback for walking, extension assist for sit-to-stand); the drive limits output torque to 19.2 N*m. Body mass is not a scenario parameter: the wearer's motion is prescribed, so it does not change the exo loads in this model.

mesh.refine: up to 3 balls {center:[x,y,z] mm, radius <= 8 mm, h >= 0.5 mm}

model_settings.note: NO may set any of these per scenario, inside the ranges; the failure must reproduce with those settings

grid.note: the judge's own coverage sweep at default model settings: 27 walking + 9 sit-to-stand scenarios

not_covered: falls, trips and impacts (the wearer's motion is prescribed, not simulated)
lateral (x) forces: the motion is planar
print defects; material values are assumed
comfort and fit on a real body
bolt preload, contact separation and friction slip at the belt clamp (the clamp is a linear elastic bond)
pass_rule: a scenario counts as a failure only if the judge reproduces it: K1, K2, S1 or S3 false. Out-of-range scenarios or settings are rejected, not run.
rule_changes: after round 2: the 2 mm boundary exclusion applies to each stress-reading point (element corner) instead of to whole elements by their centre; rounds 1 and 2 re-judged

after round 3: the rigid belt clamp (fixed face and fixed bolt bores, with a 2 mm unscored zone) is replaced by an elastic clamp (spring bed plus bolt springs), stress is read at every integration point instead of extrapolated corners, and nothing is excluded; rounds 1-3 re-judged

belt_clamp.model: linear elastic clamp: the bracket face on the belt plate (x=0 inside the plate footprint) rests on grounded springs per unit area; each M5 belt bolt is a spring in x, y and z spread over its bore by area. Values assumed: a 5 mm PA6 belt plate (E 3000 MPa, G 1100 MPa) on a rigid frame, and a steel M5 bolt bearing in the printed flange.
